title: Rolling out a release without waking everyone
summary: Release many times a day, and catch a bad release while it has touched only a few people.
context: Hoodi Hops ships 30 services from a monorepo, and a release goes to all instances at once. Twice this quarter a bad release took orders down during dinner, and rolling back took 25 minutes because the migration had already run.
Teams now avoid releasing on Fridays and in the evening, so releases pile up and get larger, which makes them riskier still.
must_handle: A release reaches a small share of traffic before the rest.
A bad release is noticed by a measure, without waiting for a person.
Rollback takes minutes, including when the schema has changed.
A service's release can wait for one it depends on.
An engineer can see at a glance what is running where.
show_in_answer: The stages of a release, and what moves it forward.
Which signals decide to stop, and how noise is told from harm.
How database changes are released so that rollback stays possible.
What on-call sees and does during a bad release.
